claims.claim: The Human Genome Project's U.S. contribution was originally projected at $3 billion and the project took about 13 years.
claims.episode_span: The Human Genome Project delivered one complete sequence at a reported cost on the order of three billion dollars after thirteen years of work.
claims.source_title: The Cost of Sequencing a Human Genome - National Human Genome Research Institute
claims.supporting_quote: The originally projected cost for the U.S.'s contribution to the HGP was $3 billion; in actuality, the Project ended up taking less time (~13 years rather than ~15 years)

claims.claim: Whole-genome sequencing has been commercially offered for around $600 - a few hundred dollars.
claims.episode_span: Today a whole human genome can be sequenced for a few hundred dollars in well under a day.
claims.supporting_quote: In summer 2019, Veritas Genetics cut the cost for WGS to $599. [ 79 ] In 2017, BGI began offering WGS for $600.

claims.claim: Sanger sequencing was developed in 1977 and remained the most widely used sequencing method for roughly 40 years.
claims.episode_span: Sanger sequencing had been the established method since the late 1970s.
claims.supporting_quote: After first being developed by Frederick Sanger and colleagues in 1977, it became the most widely used sequencing method for approximately 40 years.

claims.claim: Illumina-style sequencing uses nucleotides with reversible fluorescent blockers so bases are added one at a time and imaged in place.
claims.episode_span: cyclic addition of reversible terminators whose fluorescence could be imaged in place, eliminating the need for a separate separation step per fragment.
claims.supporting_quote: These nucleotides have a reversible fluorescent blocker, so the DNA polymerase can add only one nucleotide at a time onto the DNA fragment.

claims.claim: Massively parallel sequencing immobilizes millions of DNA fragments on a flow-cell surface, amplified into clusters by bridge amplification.
claims.episode_span: The first redesign move was to immobilize millions of separate DNA fragments on a single planar surface so that the same polymerase and nucleotide mix could act on all of them simultaneously
claims.supporting_quote: Millions of oligos line the bottom of each flow cell lane.

claims.claim: Ion semiconductor sequencing measures nucleotide incorporation directly with electronics, avoiding labeled nucleotides and optical measurement hardware.
claims.episode_span: a fourth move replaced optical cameras with semiconductor sensors built directly under the flow cell, removing the expensive objective lenses and alignment hardware
claims.supporting_quote: Because nucleotide incorporation events are measured directly by electronics, the use of labeled nucleotides and optical measurements are avoided.

claims.claim: Around the mid-2000s, sequencing a human genome with then-available (Sanger-era) approaches was estimated to cost tens of millions of dollars (about $50 million for a second reference genome; ~$14 million by 2006).
claims.episode_span: the early-2000s price for a mammalian-sized genome remained in the tens of millions of dollars when estimated by extrapolating Sanger runs.
claims.source_title: The Cost of Sequencing a Human Genome - National Human Genome Research Institute
claims.supporting_quote: NHGRI estimated that the hypothetical 2003 cost to generate a 'second' reference human genome sequence using the then-available approaches and technologies was in the neighborhood of $50 million.
